newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh has sought financial and technical assistance from the Netherlands for the construction of the proposed Ganges barrage project.
The government has postponed Thursday's scheduled repatriation of 200 Rohingya refugees following a law and order problem in camps.
About 10,000 Bangladeshi workers in Libya are not getting wages.
Thailand on Wednesday agreed to make direct investment in Bangladesh in seven sectors, including textile, shrimp and cement.
The entire country was without electricity for about 45 minutes on Wednesday, following a major disruption in national power grid.
Main opposition Bangladesh Nationaliost Party (BNP) on Wednesday protested the reported government move to remove the chief clergy of the national Batiul Mukarram mosque.
The Dutch Common Fund for Commodities is likely to arrange a revolving fund for promotion of jute fibre in world market.
Exports from the country's export processing zones registered a 37 percent rise in 1996/97 (July-June) over the previous year. REUTER
